Topic: Astrolabe – 3D Dependency Graph Visualizer for Lean 4

Hi everyone,

I've been working on Astrolabe, a tool for visualizing Lean 4 project dependencies as interactive 3D graphs.
Repo: https://github.com/Xinze-Li-Bryan/Astrolabe
Video: https://youtu.be/J9V-MpKTQpE

The demo shows some basic features I've been adding: dynamically adding verified nodes, expanding dependencies on the fly, taking notes, creating connections, customizing nodes and edges, and navigating the graph interactively.

I'm setting a goal for myself: to keep exploring new interaction patterns and visualization approaches for formal mathematics. I believe there's a lot of untapped potential in how we represent and navigate proofs.

I'd love to connect with others thinking about how to make formal mathematics more accessible and engaging. Some questions I'm exploring:

  • Visualization: How can we make formal proofs and their dependencies more visually compelling? What representations would help people actually want to explore a proof's structure?
  • AI integration: How might better interfaces accelerate AI-assisted formalization? What would an ideal human-AI workflow for theorem proving look like?
  • Collaboration & sharing: What tools would help people collaborate on formalizations, share progress, take notes, or teach formal methods more effectively?
  • Feature requests: What views or features would you want to see implemented? I'd love to know what would be most useful to prioritize.

If any of these resonate with you — whether you're into visualization, AI, education, or just want better tooling — I'd love to hear your thoughts. Happy to discuss here #general > Astrolabe - 3D dependency graph visualizer or connect directly. And thanks to everyone in the Lean community for your encouragement and feedback — it's been a big motivation to keep building.
